decisions.reason: As a new 2018 variant very close to the core cardboard display business, it is a low-cost option to keep on the market because one year reveals too little and the firm has a narrow product range worth broadening incrementally.

This pegboard-back shelf display is an incremental extension of the established offer, so real-options logic favors keeping it while market response is still uncertain and carrying costs are likely modest within existing production and sales systems.

Because this quarter-pallet cardboard display sits squarely in the firm's core competence and there is no clear negative evidence yet, management would keep the option open rather than exit after only its launch year.
This eighth-pallet format expands the firm's standard display range with limited additional commitment, so it should be retained until more demand information is available.

Although the wooden display pallet is somewhat more adjacent than the cardboard products, it still builds on the firm's display offering and should be kept for now because the firm has few innovation options and it is too early to judge its value conclusively.

This media-focused quarter-pallet display is a near-core application of existing capabilities, and with no evidence of poor results yet the firm would rationally preserve the option for another period.
